label: token right after a u at position 2 (third original token)
explanation: Fires only in the original phase, at t=2 (85% of mass) or t=3 (15%), and almost only when the previous input was u (99.9% of mass; prev_tok=u has 35x lift). It is never active at the delimiter or in the copy phase. The core predicate is t==2 after u, as in x u [y]. It also fires more weakly and less reliably at t=3 after u (x y u [z]). In the strongest examples the first token is s (s u [z] reaches max activation), and z as the current token is the most enriched. Whether it fires depends on the first token: sequences starting with m, k, 3 or h often do not fire, and leaving those out raises precision to 0.85 (dev F1 0.81). That exclusion list is ad hoc, so it is not in the predicate. Missing first-token dependence and the partial t=3 firing keep this below fully explained. Dev: P 0.76, R 0.81, F1 0.78, mass recall 0.85.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: t=2 & prev_tok=u (+12.32), t=3 & prev_tok=u (+7.17), prev_tok=u (+4.03), prev2_tok=s (+3.21), prev3_tok=r (+2.83), orig1=n (+2.55). Lower it: correct=1 (-5.23), prev2_tok=o (-3.32), orig_idx=-1 (-3.20), in_tok=x (-3.09).
